A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UNLOCK framework and benchmarks. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation experiments on K2B, A2B, and Cityscapes-to-DensePASS, together with component ablations and appendix sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a masking control, individual-threshold experiments, and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The OPLL and ADCL procedures, architecture, losses, and inference remain unchanged. ADCL-Zero names the existing zero-filling procedure in Equation 10; ADCL-Random is an added ablation control.

E1.justification: Both versions retain K2B, A2B, and Cityscapes-to-DensePASS with the same segmentation tasks. The added sensitivity tests and illustrative cases do not establish a new dataset, domain, or separately defined evaluation population.

E2.justification: The ADCL comparison adds ADCL-Random in v2 Table 7, corresponding to v1 Table 5. Existing comparators remain, and ADCL is renamed ADCL-Zero. The main benchmark comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds experiments varying one threshold while holding the others fixed, plus a control replacing overlapping regions with random values. These extend the evaluation design; retained benchmark splits, metrics, training budgets, and model configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Diagnostic evidence expands beyond v1's paired threshold sweeps: v2 isolates individual thresholds across all three branches, tests random versus zero overlap filling, and adds sparse-fence failure and object-pool case studies. Sections 9–10 therefore add distinct checks of parameter sensitivity, masking design, sample quality, and failure behavior.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without specified seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The existing mention of multiple experimentation rounds for baseline reproduction is unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds threshold-sweep results and qualitative findings while retaining existing benchmark and ablation values. Its new ADCL-Random row reports 24.81 mAPQ, compared with the retained ADCL-Zero result of 25.84. These are additional diagnostic results, not improved headline performance.

T1.justification: The task definitions and mathematical content of Equations 1–10 remain unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs; equation presentation edits do not alter the reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: introducing SFOASS, proposing UNLOCK with OPLL and ADCL, and demonstrating competitive source-free adaptation. The headline performance and novelty claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation of sparse-fence failures, further interpretations of threshold-related noise and sample trade-offs, and a potential scalability limitation involving category counts and complex occlusions. Existing limitations concerning panoramic boundaries and branch interactions remain.

D1.justification: Section 9 newly specifies that the existing sensitivity analyses isolate OPLL and ADCL separately. Section 8 also explicitly describes their operation on training data without architectural modification. These clarify documentation; hardware, core hyperparameters, and code/data release information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 100 cited works and the same positioning relative to OASS and source-free adaptation are retained. Removing a repeated Sekkat/CARLA description and rephrasing the AoMix comparison do not materially change the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and acronym edits, shortens several explanations, adds author contact and acknowledgment information, and subdivides Section 10. The overall narrative and section sequence remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds six threshold tables and Figures 12–13, exchanges the positions of the ADCL and backbone tables, and reflows existing material while preserving the visual format. Figure 13 incorrectly repeats Figure 12's failure-case caption despite showing object-pool examples.

improvement.justification: The individual-threshold experiments and random-fill control better isolate existing design choices, while the failure case and expanded limitations make applicability clearer. These provide a limited evidential improvement without changing the central method or benchmark findings. Figure 13's incorrect caption is a localized presentation drawback.
